project: IGCSE ESL — Mr Evans English (design decks)
purpose: Source and wire real photographs into the <image-slot> placeholders in the slide decks. Same convention as the Year 8 Suspense decks; the ART DIRECTION is different (see below).

art_direction.look: Contemporary documentary photography of real, everyday PLACES WHERE PEOPLE GATHER. Warm, natural light. Honest, un-staged — not glossy stock. This course is about belonging and modern life, so the register is bright and human, NOT the dark/quiet suspense register.
art_direction.geography: Lead with Southeast / East Asia where the texts are set (Bangkok study cafés, Japanese/Thai konbini, SE-Asian malls, city street corners), then broaden per unit theme. Keep it globally recognisable to teenage students.
art_direction.people: No identifiable faces. Figures may be distant, from behind, in silhouette, blurred with motion, or implied by their things (an empty chair, a laptop, a cup). Nothing that reads as a named person; no children's faces.
art_direction.content_limits: Nothing that would be unsafe on a classroom projector: no alcohol focus, no logos as the subject, no distress imagery. Everyday, calm, inviting.
art_direction.composition: Full-bleed crops behind or beside text. Prefer clear negative space and one strong subject. Title/context slots are tall portrait panels (~640–760 × 1080).

allowed_sources: Wikimedia Commons — public domain or CC0 only
licensing.forbidden: Anything CC BY-NC, CC BY-SA, rights-managed, watermarked, or scraped from Google Images / Pinterest / brand marketing.
licensing.record: For every file, append a row to assets/IMAGE-CREDITS.md: slot id, filename, source URL, licence, photographer/collection, date retrieved.
licensing.format: JPEG, sRGB, long edge 2400px, quality ~80, under 600KB each. Filenames must equal the slot id (e.g. u1-opener-hero.jpg).

wiring.how: Each placeholder is <image-slot id="…" placeholder="…"></image-slot>. Save files to assets/images/<slot-id>.jpg and add src="assets/images/<slot-id>.jpg" to the matching tag. Do not remove id/shape/fit, and do not change any other markup, styling or copy in the deck.
wiring.constraint: Every slide is a fixed 1920×1080 box and must measure exactly 1080px tall — do not add or resize any element. Images fill existing containers via object-fit: cover only.

slots.container: ~640×1080 vertical panel, right of the title
slots.brief: Unit cover: a warm, busy 'third place' — a study café at golden hour, a lit konbini at night, or a mall food court. Sense of belonging, people present but faces not identifiable.
search_terms: mall food court people from above

slots.brief: One quiet detail that says 'a place that is neither home nor school' — an empty café corner table with a laptop, a bench by a shop window, a single occupied seat.
Contemporary, student-recognisable: teenagers (from behind / distant) gathering somewhere ordinary — outside a convenience store, on library steps, at a mall.
search_terms: teenagers convenience store evening back view

slots.brief: Orientation mood: an ordinary, welcoming 'third place' where people gather — a bench outside a shop, a café corner, library steps. Warm daylight, inviting, faces not identifiable.
A study café: long desks, soft lamps, a power socket at every seat, students with headphones — quiet, focused. Faces not identifiable.
Bangkok/Seoul café context: a calm café interior at study time; one drink, a notebook, exam-season quiet.
'My Corner' mood: a small crooked corner table in warm, golden, dusty afternoon light. Belonging, atmosphere. No people or one distant figure.
search_terms: cafe corner table golden afternoon light

slots.brief: Sensory detail — a chipped cup, worn wooden table, light through a café window. For teaching 'reading for feeling'.
A characterful place worth describing — a corner café with a window seat, warm light, plants, a worn wooden table. Detail-rich (adjectives to notice), faces not identifiable.
search_terms: corner cafe window seat warm light

slots.brief: A 24-hour convenience store (konbini / 7-Eleven) glowing at night, seen from the street; or a window counter with stools. Faces not identifiable.
The konbini as living room: seats by the window, a microwave, snacks; small comforts that turn a stop into a stay.
People gathering in an everyday public place — a library reading room, a lit shop corner at night, friends on steps. Warm, documentary, sense of listening/conversation. Faces not identifiable.
A daily-routine feel at a gathering place — a regular's usual seat, a morning coffee ritual, someone settled into a familiar spot with their things. Warm, everyday. Faces not identifiable.
A big air-conditioned SE-Asian shopping mall — atrium, escalators, food court from above. Busy but faces not identifiable.
The mall as free social space: a bench by a fountain, teenagers gathered at a food-court table (from behind).
A place worth reviewing — an inviting independent café or study spot with real character: a menu/chalkboard, warm light, a good window seat, plants. Faces not identifiable.
A closed-down corner shop/arcade: papered-over windows, a 'closing/opening soon' sign, an empty street corner. Quiet loss — but daylight, not sinister.
Gentrification detail: a 'premium café opening soon' hoarding, a 'no loitering' sign, a bench removed. Everyday, understated.
A lively public place where people gather and talk — a busy square, market, community space, or steps full of people. Sense of belonging and debate. Warm, faces not identifiable.
Unit 2 cover: a striking natural landscape or living thing — a lush wetland at dawn, a migrating flock, a mountain valley. Alive, warm natural light, no identifiable faces.

A person (from behind / distant) in nature — planting, watching wildlife, walking a green space; or a close detail of a threatened local species/habitat. Contemporary, hopeful, faces not identifiable.
Orientation mood: an inviting, alive natural place — a green wetland, a forest clearing, a tide pool teeming with life. Warm daylight, no identifiable faces.
A rich natural scene packed with life — a coral reef, a rainforest layer, or a meadow full of insects and flowers. Suggests variety and abundance. No identifiable faces.
A strange, striking plant — a desert welwitschia, a giant titan arum bloom, or an otherworldly succulent. Extraordinary, a little uncanny. No identifiable faces.
An extraordinary survival adaptation in close-up — a desert plant storing water, a strange bloom, a resurrection plant curled dry then green. Uncanny, detailed. No identifiable faces.
A great animal migration — a huge flock of birds, a herd of wildebeest crossing a plain, or a whale breaching. Epic scale, movement. No identifiable faces.
Migration in motion — a flock crossing the sky, wildebeest fording a river, or terns over the sea. Sense of a vast journey. No identifiable faces.
Two contrasting landscapes side by side, or one scene with clear contrast — desert meeting green, mountain and valley, still and moving water. Invites comparison. No identifiable faces.
search_terms: arid and lush side by side

slots.brief: A restored river or wetland full of life — clear water, reeds, a dragonfly, an otter or heron. Hopeful, healthy, warm light. No identifiable faces.
A community caring for a river — volunteers planting reeds or clearing a bank (distant/from behind), or a clean river with reeds. Hopeful, everyday. No identifiable faces.
search_terms: volunteers river clean up back view

slots.brief: A green rooftop farm above a city — vegetable beds on a roof with tower blocks behind. Green against grey concrete. No identifiable faces.
A rooftop vegetable garden in a dense city — beds of greens and herbs with skyline behind, or hands tending a rooftop bed (from behind). Green among concrete. No identifiable faces.
A field-report feel — a scientist's notebook and measurements by a river, a monitoring station, or a clipboard and sample jars. Neutral, factual. No identifiable faces.
A listening-in-nature feel — headphones and a notebook by a window onto greenery, or a person (from behind) listening at a nature reserve. Calm, focused. No identifiable faces.
search_terms: person listening nature reserve back view

slots.deck: U2 L10 A Letter About Nature
slots.brief: A natural place worth writing home about — a wetland at dawn, a forest, a wild coast, birds lifting off water. Alive, warm light, no identifiable faces.
A place a report might save — a neglected river or green space that could be restored, or a restored one thriving. Hopeful, civic. No identifiable faces.
Unit 3 cover: everyday wellbeing — someone walking or stretching in morning light, fresh food on a table, or a calm tidy space. Warm, human, healthy. No identifiable faces.
Students collaborating on a project / making a simple wellbeing poster — hands, markers, sticky notes. Collaborative and positive. No identifiable faces.
Orientation mood: a calm, healthy everyday moment — morning light on a made bed, a walk, a glass of water and fruit. Warm, ordinary, inviting. No identifiable faces.
